steps.body: Distance problems repeat a fractional length: six laps of 3/8 mile covers 18/8 miles, which is 2 1/4.
steps.narration: Distance problems repeat a fractional length: six laps of 3/8 mile covers 18/8 miles, which is 2 1/4.

widget.prompt: On an EIGHTHS line, place where 2 × 3/8 lands.

commonPlacements.feedback: 3/8 is a single lap. Two were run.
8/8 is a full mile; two laps of 3/8 stop short of it.

widget.successFeedback: 6/8 — two jumps of three eighths, landing three quarters of the way to one.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — each lap covers three eighths, so two laps reach six of them.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — two laps of three eighths stop at 6/8, short of the full mile.

predict.prompt: Six laps of 3/8 mile — total distance?
predict.reveal: Six groups of three eighths is eighteen eighths; nine would be only three laps.

cml.actionGoal: Collect equal groups of a fraction and watch only the COUNT of pieces change for g4x distance.
invariants: Multiplying a fraction by a whole number collects groups of identical pieces: the denominator names the piece size and holds still, while the numerator counts every piece gathered, which is what keeps g4x distance a counting problem.
misconceptions: Scaling the denominator along with the numerator, adding the whole number to the numerator, or assuming a product cannot pass one whole.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the denominator DID change when you collected groups, what would happen to the size of each piece?

widget.prompt: A runner covers 3/8 mile per lap and runs 6 laps. Which computes the distance?

options.label: 6 × 3/8 = 18/8 miles
options.feedback: Correct — six equal laps of three eighths each collects eighteen eighths, or 2 1/4 miles.

options.label: 6 + 3/8 miles
options.feedback: Adding treats the lap count as a distance; six equal laps calls for multiplication.

options.label: 6 ÷ 3/8 miles
options.feedback: Dividing asks how many laps fit in six miles — a different question entirely.

options.label: 3/8 mile, since each lap is the same
options.feedback: That is one lap. Six were run, so the distance is six times as far.

widget.prompt: Diagnose a new distance: which computes 5 laps of 2/8 mile?

options.label: 5 × 2/8 = 10/8 miles

options.feedback: The 5 counts laps; it is not itself a distance to add.

options.feedback: That asks how many two-eighth-mile lengths fit in five miles.

options.label: 2/8 mile because every lap matches
options.feedback: That is one lap; the total includes all five laps.

widget.prompt: A swimmer completes 4 laps of 3/10 kilometre. Which computes the total distance?

options.label: 4 × 3/10 = 12/10 kilometres
options.feedback: Correct — four equal laps collect twelve tenths of a kilometre.

options.label: 4 + 3/10 kilometres
options.feedback: Four counts laps, not kilometres to add directly.

options.label: 4 ÷ 3/10 kilometres
options.feedback: That asks how many fractional lengths fit into four kilometres.

options.label: 3/10 kilometre
options.feedback: That is one lap; include all four laps.
